new_statements.relation_note: Segmental key (b/ph variants across Poswoy, Mabaca, Buaya, Lubuagan; glottal stop unmarked before vowels, weak intervocalically; l as [l]; aspirated g; vowels i, o, a (+schwa in some dialects); diphthongs ei, oi, ao, oa, yu) plus the single stress/length sentence quoted; cites Gieser 1958 and Scheerer 1921 for comparison.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Author states stress was not analysed but that stress, together with vowel length, distinguishes meaning in some forms (minimal pair apo: 'grandparents' vs a:po 'grandchildren'), i.e. stress/length is lexically contrastive in the Northern Kalinga (Mabaca/Poswoy) speech he recorded; no default position is given.
new_statements.exceptions: none; explicitly 'has not been studied'; only one minimal pair cited
new_statements.identity_note: Dozier's 'Northern Kalinga' = the Mabaca and Poswoy regions of Balbalan municipal district (Mabaca, Buaya, Tawang, Poswoy, Daoangan, Ababaan barrios in his population tables). The Mabaca valley/river (Balbalan, flowing north to Conner, Apayao) is the eponymous home of Mabaka Valley Kalinga [kkg]; Poswoy lies on the Saltan near Salegseg (Ethnologue groups Ableg-Salegseg with Lubuagan/Limos-area Kalinga), so the key mixes kkg (Mabaca) with an adjacent Northern Kalinga variety and also notes Lubuagan and Salegseg variants. Not a namesake: same province, same river valley, Kalinga-Itneg, and the SIL kkg wordlists' 'Mataragan' informants belong to the same Mabaka group. | group-level statement: 'Kalinga' in Zorc's accent classification is generic (his Kalinga data come from Guinaang/Limos SIL sources); Mabaka Valley Kalinga is not named individually [name in source: Kalinga (variety unspecified); pages 20 (Table 2, class A)]

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word accent (realised chiefly as penult vowel length) is contrastive/lexical in Kalinga, as in Ilokano, Tagalog etc; not predictable by position.
new_statements.exceptions: none for Kalinga; general remark that stress has low functional load on closed penults (CVC.CV(C))
